newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Nervous Belgian bonds treck higher awaiting news.
newsitem.headline: Nervous Belgian bonds treck higher awaiting news.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds moved higher in thin volume in morning trade on Tuesday, waiting for U.S. consumer price data in the afternoon and held in check by the forthcoming OLO exchange auction, traders said.
"We are moving up in line with other European markets. It is a technical rebound," one trader said.

"We are underperforming Bunds a bit, but that is normal on days with exchange auctions. If there is a decent CPI this afternoon then we will spend the rest of the week moving up before turning lower again next week," he added.
The March CPI figures, due at 1230 GMT, are expected to show a month-on-month rise of 0.2 percent and a year-on-year increase
Higher figures could fuel feelings that the U.S. Federal Reserve will again raise interest rates to stamp out any signs of inflationary brush fires.
However, traders said rate rises up 50 basis points are already priced into the bond markets and would therefore have no negative impact.
Of more immediate interest is the OLO exchange auction due later on Tuesday.

The Belgian Treasury is exchanging OLO line 4 (9.25 pct, Jan 1998) for OLO 13 (7.00 pct, April 1999), 25 (5.00 pct, March 2001), 6 (9.00 pct, March 2003), 19 (6.50 pct, March 2005) and 26 (6.25 pct March 2007).
There is also a regular Treasury bill auction today.
Traders said they were unsure how the auction would go because people were nervous of adding to their positions before the market definitively picked a direction.
"Most people are afraid of taking paper at the moment. Everybody is waiting and watching. Only once the market starts to move will any real trading resume," one trader said.
At 0845 GMT the yield on the benchmark March 2007 OLO BE286= was 6.03 percent, down from Monday's late 6.06.
As OLOs lagged Bunds on the way up, the 10-year spread over Bunds widened to 13 basis points from 11.
The June OLO future was 30 basis points higher at 119.90 in a volume of 311 contracts.
